claims.text: Mg-transition-metal powder mixtures are prone to elemental segregation and unstable microstructures because solid-state diffusion is limited at low sintering temperatures.
Magnesium has high volatility at elevated sintering temperatures.
Transition-metal dithiocarbamates can be thermally decomposed under argon as a molecular-precursor synthesis route.
Co-dissolving metal salts and dithiocarbamate ligands will create a homogeneous Mg-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni precursor mixture.
A molecular-precursor route will achieve atomic-scale mixing and suppress elemental segregation in the proposed Mg-transition-metal alloy.
Argon will prevent premature oxidation during sintering.
An argon atmosphere will manage magnesium volatility during sintering.
Atomic-scale precursor mixing eliminates the diffusion distance normally required to homogenize mechanically mixed powders.
Bypassing solid-state diffusion barriers will permit a metastable solid solution or single-phase-like structure to form at a lower thermal budget.
Sintering the precursor-derived Mg-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni material at 900 °C will produce a dense, single-phase-like microstructure.
Enhanced diffusion kinetics at 900 °C will allow the precursor-derived alloy to reach greater than 95% relative density.
The resulting alloy will have a density below 6 g/cm³.
A uniform distribution of chromium or other protective-oxide-forming elements will significantly improve oxidation and corrosion barrier properties.
Standard mechanical powder mixing followed by sintering in the 800–1000 °C regime produces insufficient density or requires temperatures that cause porosity and elemental volatility.
Standard powder processing in this regime leads to segregated phases and poor barrier properties.
Relative density falls below 90% when the sintering temperature is below 850 °C.
Magnesium loss exceeds 5% when the sintering temperature exceeds 1000 °C.
A slow heating rate can cause excessive magnesium loss by allowing magnesium vapor pressure to build before densification.
The single-phase rationale for the proposed Mg-based system is extrapolated from non-Mg CoCrFeNi-family alloys.
